assumptions_or_open_questions: Sub-adult stage: the current model has only adults and juveniles. Adding a sub-adult stage requires deciding whether sub-adults can reproduce (likely no) and how maturation_accum splits across two transitions (juvenile→sub-adult, sub-adult→adult). The design note must propose concrete transition criteria.

Per-stage vs single-pool condition: currently condition_index, molt_stress_index, and reproductive_readiness_index are single scalars for the whole population. Should each stage cohort carry its own condition/reserve, or is a population-wide average acceptable for the stage-structured model? The backlog recommends 'aggregate metrics per stage' — the design note should specify which indices are per-stage and which remain global.

Reserve partitioning: reserve_g is currently a single pool. With three life stages, should reserve be split per-stage (so juveniles don't fund adult reproduction)? This affects the routing contract in ROUTING.md.

Molt interval as explicit state: the current model has molt_stress_index but no explicit inter-molt timer or last-molt-success flag. Adding these as state fields requires deciding the molt cycle period (species-dependent, ~4-6 weeks for Neocaridina) and whether failed molts accumulate or reset.

Backward compatibility: existing save files have the flat AnimalState. The design note should specify a migration strategy (runtime upgrade on deserialization with serde defaults, similar to egg_cohorts migration).
What remains intentionally omitted: sex ratio, individual tracking, size-within-stage variation, predation, disease. The bead explicitly asks for these omission notes.
Clutch size variability: currently fixed at 25 juveniles_per_clutch. Should the design note propose condition-dependent clutch size, or defer that to implementation?
data.problem_framing: The current AnimalState in biology.rs tracks shrimp as a flat struct with adults_count, juveniles_count, berried_females_count, three condition indices, egg cohorts, stress accumulators, and a reserve pool. The bead requests a design note that restructures this into an explicit stage-structured cohort model with reserve/condition, life stages (juvenile, sub-adult, adult), molt state, and reproduction state — while maintaining the population-level (not individual-based) abstraction. The documentation ecosystem already has prescriptive contracts (ROUTING.md, UNITS.md, carbonate_state_contract.md) and a descriptive inventory (scientific_inventory.md). The new design note must follow the same pattern: prescriptive contract that downstream implementation beads (especially F2/tanksim-6e5.6.2) can code against without reworking the model. The main documentation deliverable is a new docs/shrimp_state_contract.md plus updates to scientific_inventory.md to flag the upcoming state redesign.

proposed_work.details: Write the primary deliverable: a prescriptive contract document following the same structure as carbonate_state_contract.md. Sections: (1) Chosen state model — stage-structured cohort with three stages (juvenile, sub-adult, adult) plus berried-adult subset; (2) Reserve and condition — per-stage reserve_g, per-stage condition_index, population-wide food intake converted to per-stage allocation; (3) Life stages — stage definitions, transition criteria (days + condition thresholds), maturation accumulators per transition; (4) Molt state — inter-molt interval timer, molt readiness derived from GH/condition/reserve, last_molt_success boolean, failed-molt penalty accumulator; (5) Reproduction — egg-carrying state (berried females as subset of adults), clutch size (base + condition modifier), incubation progress via EggCohort, hatch success factors; (6) Population vs individual boundary — explicit statement that this is a stage-structured population model (Leslie/Lefkovitch matrix family), no individual tracking, aggregate metrics per stage; (7) Intentional omissions — sex ratio (implicit 50:50), individual identity, size-within-stage, predation, disease, genetic variation; (8) Extension points — hooks for future habitat-aware grazing, mineral budget for molting, toxicity modifiers; (9) Migration strategy — serde default-based runtime upgrade from flat AnimalState; (10) Downstream bead map — which implementation beads consume this contract.
proposed_work.summary: Create docs/shrimp_state_contract.md — the prescriptive design note

risks: The per-stage reserve split decision (single pool vs per-stage) has routing implications. If the design note chooses per-stage reserves, the ROUTING.md consumer template will need a more substantial update than a simple cross-reference. Mitigation: the design note should clearly state whether per-stage reserve is phase-1 or deferred.

The sub-adult stage is not present in any existing code or test. The design note must be specific enough about sub-adult behavior that F2 implementers don't need to re-derive the contract, but flexible enough that tuning parameters can change. Mitigation: specify the structure and transition rules, but make thresholds configurable via ShrimpRuntimeParams.

Existing save-file migration: the design note proposes serde-default migration, but if the struct shape changes dramatically (e.g., nested per-stage substruct), simple defaults may not suffice. Mitigation: the design note should specify the exact new struct layout so migration feasibility is clear before implementation begins.
